dimensions.name: Contract & reference orientation

evidence.note: Solid opening orientation: inventoried workspace, cat'd all Cargo.tomls, grepped rusternetes imports across tests, and read common/storage/scheduler/kubectl tests to identify referenced APIs before coding.

The ONLY consultation of /opt/k8s-reference — a single grep for IPAddress/ServiceCIDR structs that returned nothing (reference is Go). The agent noted 'grep in Kubernetes reference did not find direct Rust structs' and never consulted the reference again in ~419 subsequent steps.

Contract inference done purely by reading tests and chasing compiler errors (Option vs non-Option, field names, condition fields), not from the reference — establishing the fixture-fitting pattern that dominates the run.

Repeated field-name/type guessing contradicted by test failures: removing 'extra'/'type_'/'cluster_i_ps' fields, flipping Option-ness — the level-3 'repeatedly guesses field names later contradicted by test failures' failure mode sustained throughout.

Late-trajectory churn (NodeStats/EvictionThreshold/HPA fields added then removed to satisfy struct literals; csinode breakage from earlier type changes) shows the reference was never mined for genuine k8s semantics; conformance suite never considered.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent reads each crate's tests systematically and respects the leaf-to-root dependency graph (both above anchor 3), but it consulted the mounted v1.35 upstream reference exactly once with no result and never again, driving all contract inference by test-reading plus compiler-error-chasing and repeatedly guessing field shapes that tests later contradict — the hallmark level-3 behavior. It never consults the reference for the specific behaviors a crate is tested on (the level-5 requirement) and never reasons about the hidden conformance suite. This places it solidly between anchors 3 and 5, landing at 4: better-than-3 test mining and dependency-order awareness, but pure fixture-fitting with the reference effectively ignored.

dimensions.name: Leaf-to-root crate sequencing & milestones

evidence.note: Leaf-first intent stated ('Start with the leaf crates'); common crate treated as a real milestone — iterated to compile, then verified all 34 tests pass as an explicit done-check before advancing.

Named storage as 'next target' but immediately switched to full `cargo test --workspace --tests --no-run`, collapsing the plan into a single workspace-wide compile-error queue rather than a per-crate storage milestone.

Sustained monolithic pattern: fixes chase whatever error the workspace build emits next — kubectl, api-server, scheduler affinity, controller-manager, kubelet CNI all interleaved with no crate-ordered milestones or per-crate exit criteria.

Still patching individual struct-field mismatches against the whole-workspace build at the very end; no sub-milestone decomposition of large crates (e.g. api-server), no TodoWrite/milestone tracking, never reaches a per-crate green checkpoint beyond common.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent exceeds anchor 3 (vague intent) because it explicitly ordered leaf-first and applied a genuine 'compiles + tests pass' done-check to the common crate. But it falls short of anchor 5's sustained per-crate milestone discipline: only common received that treatment, after which the remaining ~400 steps became an undifferentiated workspace-wide compile-error chase with no per-crate exit criteria, no sub-milestones inside large crates, and no dependency-aware milestone plan. Judged over the whole horizon, the strong start does not offset the abandoned structure, placing it at a 4.

dimensions.name: Incremental & semantic verification

evidence.note: Early tight per-crate loop: compiles common with --no-run, drives fixes off compiler errors, gets leaf crate to green and tracks exact pass counts ('17/18', '34 tests pass'). Genuine test-pass verification at the leaf level.
Shifts to repeated `cargo test --workspace --tests --no-run` piped to /tmp logs, patching off compile errors. Incremental and periodic, but the bar is 'does it compile', not 'do provided tests pass'.
Only two `--no-fail-fast` runtime test attempts; both immediately surfaced compile errors and reverted to fixing. Agent never reaches a green workspace to verify provided suites at scale.
Targeted per-test compiles (`--test csinode_handler_test --no-run`) show disciplined triage, but purely at compile level; trajectory ends still fighting compile errors.

Touches /opt/k8s-reference exactly once, finds Go not Rust, abandons it. No independent semantic checks, no booting all-in-one binary, no HTTP/JSON conformance reasoning, no prescribed thread/skip settings anywhere.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent builds and runs tests continuously and per-crate, getting the leaf crate green while tracking counts, and runs the workspace suite periodically — matching anchor 5's 'builds/runs as it goes, treats green as the bar.' However, the loop is overwhelmingly compile-only (91 --no-run vs ~2 runtime runs) and it never reaches a green workspace to verify the provided suites at scale. Critically, it shows zero conformance/semantic verification — no booting the all-in-one binary, no HTTP/JSON checks, no prescribed thread/skip regime, and it abandons the reference tree — so it falls well short of anchor 8 and lands at 5.

dimensions.name: Test-count & horizon tracking

evidence.note: Tracks concrete leaf-crate test counts: '17/18 IPAddress tests pass', 'all its crate-local tests pass (34 tests)' — genuine per-crate pass tracking early on.
Detects a regression in the previously-green common crate after ParentReference.generate_name change and repairs it before continuing — regression awareness.
Recognizes self-inflicted oscillation on ReplicaSetStatus ('changed too many fields', flipping fields back to Option) — but only reactively via compile failure, no ledger to prevent it.
Repeated type flip-flopping on VolumeSnapshot and csinode ('Earlier csinode compiled, but later type changes likely broke it') shows circular churn caught only after the compiler re-breaks it.
End of trajectory still chasing 'current' compile errors binary-by-binary; never completed a full test run, so no test-count tally of the 100-binary/1390-test horizon ever existed.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent maintains a moderate, compile-space picture of progress — it tracks per-crate build/blocking status, cites leaf-crate pass counts (34/34, 17/18), and catches regressions in the previously-green common crate — which exceeds anchor 3's purely qualitative sense. But it never established a running tally of tests passing vs. remaining across the 1,390-test horizon (it never finished a test run), tracked progress only as 'which binary is currently failing to compile,' and repeatedly oscillated on the same struct fields (HPA, ReplicaSetStatus, VolumeSnapshot, csinode), recognizing the circularity only reactively rather than naming thrashing or reprioritizing. That places it below anchor 5's 'roughly how much of the suite is green,' landing at 4.

dimensions.name: Course-correction on falsified assumptions

evidence.note: Reversed a just-made IPAddress.spec (Option vs non-optional) decision immediately after compiler evidence contradicted it — clean local course-correction.
Recognized the SPDY channel design (struct of u8 constants) was categorically wrong vs test expectations and rewrote the whole module as an enum — anchor-8 whole-approach rework citing test usage.
Backed out the CniRuntime API assumption and replaced the entire CNI module when constructor arity/return types proved wrong.

After ResourceRequirements.claims repeatedly conflicted across suites, concluded two distinct types were needed (typed vs volume-local) — a real model correction, but only after several add/remove oscillations (151,178,242).
Reworked the admission-webhook subsystem and split ResourceMetricSource into a separate status type once designs were falsified — repeated anchor-8 reworks.

Broad text replacement injected generate_name into ParentReference, re-breaking the passing common crate; took several attempts to localize and revert — self-inflicted regression showing imperfect model-building.

Recurring oscillation: PolicyRule Option↔Vec, NodeCondition String↔DateTime, and repeatedly re-adding phase/observed_generation fields removed by broad replaces — evidence it often failed to convert contradictions into a stable model.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent reliably clears the anchor-5 bar (constantly updating wrong signatures/fields/semantics revealed by the compiler and adjusting nearby code) and reaches anchor-8 on multiple occasions — recognizing whole designs are wrong (SPDY, CNI, admission webhook, ResourceMetricSource split, dual ResourceRequirements) and backing out to rework them, plus resequencing to targeted per-test builds when full builds became blocking. It falls short of a clean 8 and well short of 10 because of pervasive oscillation and self-inflicted regressions (claims added/removed repeatedly, phase/observed_generation re-removed by broad replaces, PolicyRule and NodeCondition flip-flops), showing it frequently failed to convert contradictory evidence into a durable model. This lands squarely between the 5 and 8 anchors, at 6.

rubric.task_read: An extreme long-horizon software build: reimplement ten interdependent Kubernetes crates in Rust from stubs, with a load-bearing public API, 1,390 provided integration tests across 100 binaries, plus a hidden HTTP conformance suite demanding real k8s semantics. Difficulty comes from scale, tight cross-crate contracts inferred from tests + a pinned upstream reference, and the fact that passing visible fixtures is necessary but not sufficient. A skilled practitioner would invest heavily and continuously in orientation, sequencing (leaf→root), incremental verification, and course-correction — meta-work here is decisive, not optional.

dimensions.name: Contract & reference orientation
dimensions.description: Reading the tests, stubs, Cargo manifests, and the mounted v1.35 upstream reference to infer the exact API contracts and k8s semantics before and while implementing each crate.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The public API (type names, signatures, JSON field names, storage-key formats, watch/status semantics) is load-bearing and only partially discoverable from stubs; the hidden conformance suite punishes fixture-fitting. Acting without grounding each crate in the tests and the reference guarantees churn and shallow, non-conformant implementations.

anchors.0: Starts editing src stubs with no reading of the provided tests, manifests, or the /opt/k8s-reference tree; invents APIs.
anchors.3: Skims one crate's tests before coding it; ignores the upstream reference and the cross-crate dependency graph; repeatedly guesses field names later contradicted by test failures.
anchors.5: Reads each crate's tests and Cargo.toml before implementing it, and consults the reference for the specific behaviors that crate is tested on; understands the workspace dependency order.
anchors.8: Systematically mines tests AND the upstream reference to reconstruct contracts (camelCase JSON, /registry key format, status subresources, watch semantics); maps the whole cross-crate API surface up front and notes where the hidden conformance suite implies behavior beyond the fixtures.
anchors.10: Sustained, source-of-truth-driven investigation throughout: builds and continually refines an accurate model of k8s v1.35 semantics from the reference, proactively distinguishing test-visible contracts from genuine conformance requirements, and re-consulting the reference whenever a new behavior surfaces rather than pattern-matching fixtures.

dimensions.name: Leaf-to-root crate sequencing & milestones
dimensions.description: Breaking the ten-crate build into an ordered set of milestones (respecting the dependency DAG, leaf crates first) each with an explicit done-check, rather than one undifferentiated push.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With ~1,390 tests across 100 binaries and strong inter-crate dependencies, order determines whether progress compounds or stalls; a downstream crate cannot be verified until its dependencies compile and pass. Milestone structure is the only way to keep a task this large tractable.

anchors.0: No plan; edits arbitrary crates in arbitrary order; attempts everything at once.
anchors.3: Vague intent to 'do the crates'; no explicit ordering by dependency; no per-milestone completion criteria.
anchors.5: Follows the suggested leaf-first order (common → storage → api-server → …) with per-crate 'compiles + its tests pass' as the milestone check.
anchors.8: Explicit dependency-aware milestone plan for all ten crates with concrete exit criteria per crate, sub-milestones inside large crates (e.g. api-server: types→storage wiring→handlers→watches), and gating each layer on the prior layer being green.
anchors.10: A living, hierarchical plan that sequences work to maximize compounding progress, isolates high-risk crates early, decomposes each large crate into independently verifiable units with crisp done-checks, and is continually re-ordered as dependency realities and test-failure clusters reveal the true critical path.

dimensions.name: Incremental & semantic verification
dimensions.description: Deliberately using cargo build/test per-crate and workspace-wide, plus reasoning about the hidden conformance suite, to confirm correctness rather than assuming it.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Grading is pass/fail on every non-skipped provided test AND a hidden HTTP conformance suite; self-written tests don't count. The agent must verify continuously against the provided suites while also engineering for real k8s semantics it cannot see — a verification challenge beyond just running the given tests.

anchors.0: Never builds or runs tests; declares crates done by inspection.
anchors.3: Runs cargo build/test only sporadically or only at the very end, so failures pile up undiagnosed.
anchors.5: Builds and runs each crate's provided tests as it goes and the workspace suite periodically, treating a green provided suite as the bar.
anchors.8: Tight verify loop per milestone (build → targeted crate tests → workspace --no-fail-fast), tracks exact pass/fail counts, and deliberately reasons about conformance behavior not covered by visible fixtures (booting the all-in-one binary, checking HTTP/JSON semantics) so it doesn't just fixture-fit.
anchors.10: A rigorous, layered verification regime: fast per-unit checks feeding workspace-wide runs with the prescribed thread/skip settings, systematic triage of failure clusters, AND independent semantic checks against the upstream reference to guard the hidden conformance suite — catching over-fitting that would pass visible tests yet fail conformance.

dimensions.name: Test-count & horizon tracking
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate picture of which crates/tests pass vs. remain across ~1,390 tests, and detecting stuck/circular states rather than losing the plot.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The horizon is enormous; without an accurate running tally of done-vs-remaining and detection of thrashing (re-debugging the same crate, regressions in already-green crates), the agent will lose orientation, repeat work, or quit while wrongly believing it is close.

anchors.0: No sense of overall progress; cannot say which crates pass or how many tests remain.
anchors.3: Rough qualitative sense ('common seems done'); doesn't notice regressions or repeated failures.
anchors.5: Tracks per-crate pass/fail status and roughly how much of the suite is green; notices when a crate is stuck.
anchors.8: Maintains a concrete, updated ledger of pass counts per test binary and remaining work, watches for regressions in previously-green crates after downstream edits, and flags when it is looping on the same failure.
anchors.10: Continuous, accurate accounting across the full 100-binary horizon: distinguishes real forward progress from churn, detects circular debugging early and names it, and reprioritizes based on where the largest verified gains remain — never mistaking local activity for global progress.

dimensions.name: Course-correction on falsified assumptions
dimensions.description: Revising the implementation approach, inferred contract, or crate ordering when build/test evidence contradicts expectations, instead of barrelling ahead.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Many contracts are inferred and will be wrong; some crates will prove harder or more entangled than expected. The ability to abandon a falsified API assumption or resequence when a dependency blocks progress is what separates sustained progress from thrashing on a dead approach.

anchors.0: Repeats the same failing approach unchanged despite persistent errors; never revisits assumptions.
anchors.3: Makes only local patch-the-error fixes; doesn't reconsider a wrong contract or bad ordering even when failures cluster.
anchors.5: When a test reveals a wrong signature/field/semantic, updates the implementation and adjusts nearby work accordingly.
anchors.8: Recognizes when a whole approach or inferred contract is wrong (not just a typo), backs out and reworks it, and reorders remaining crates when a dependency proves blocking — citing the test/reference evidence that triggered the change.
anchors.10: Fluid, evidence-driven adaptation across the horizon: detects systemic mistakes early, cleanly abandons falsified designs before sinking more cost, revises the plan and re-verifies affected downstream crates, and consistently converts contradictory evidence into a better model rather than defending the original path.
